thread:
tom: Heads-up: SDK v2.14 is rolling out to hosted today (gradual). Main change: `strict_output_mode` is now the default for generation/chat/structured endpoints. 

lina: What does strict_output_mode do exactly?

tom: lina: it enforces the structured output/schema contract more tightly: trims injected separators, validates required keys in json-mode, and returns a structured parse error instead of best-effort fallback when validation fails.

priya: Why flip the default now? Any breaking customer impact?

tom: We flipped after internal & partner testing showed fewer silent data regressions and more consistent downstream parsing. Most customers on structured outputs will see fewer post-processing errors. But apps that relied on permissive fallback behavior may see parse errors where they previously got heuristically-corrected responses.

lina: Migration story?

tom: migration guide: https://redwood.dev/docs/sdk/releases/v2.14/strict-output-migration 
- If you want old behavior, set `strict_output_mode=false` in client config or use env `REDWOOD_SDK_STRICT_OUTPUT=false` until 2025-10-15.
- We recommend adding a quick test: call endpoint with representative prompts and assert parse succeeds.

priya: How about Dedicated/Private?

tom: Dedicated customers can opt their pools with runtime flag `permissive_output=true` for 120 days. Private installs get the patch but default is unchanged until operators toggled it. See the private repo notice sent to operators.

qa-bot: Note: SDK unit tests updated, 18 failing tests fixed across starter-repo PRs.

deploy-bot: docs: published v2.14 release notes + migration guide  status: live :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Created KB ticket #KB-1599 "Strict output mode default change" and assigned to Support Docs, ETA 4 business days.

lina: Telemetry/alerts we should watch?

tom: We've added metric `sdk.strict_output.parse_errors` and an internal dashboard. We'll alert if parse_errors spike >5x baseline for any org in 1h. Also logging will include `strict_output` tag.

priya: Any quick code examples for JS?

tom: paste: 
```
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood.Client({ strict_output_mode: false })
const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-2b', prompt: '...' })
```

lina: Action items recap: 
- Docs: migration guide live (done)
- Support: KB ticket (#KB-1599)
- Eng/ops: Dedicated pool flag staged
- Private: operator patch in private repo + operator notice sent

priya: We'll send a short broadcast to customers with >100k structured calls.

tom: Thanks all. If you own integrations/examples, please update starters or pin to v2.13 if you need permissive behavior before 2025-10-15. Ping me for rollouts. :shipit:
